Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Expectation2: Ensure compliance with tax laws and regulations.
Situation2: A notice has just arrived from the tax authority indicating a discrepancy that requires an immediate response.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was sorting through a stack of invoices, my mind already racing from the tax notice that had landed on my desk minutes earlier. The subject line—“Immediate Action Required”—still glared at me from my computer screen, a stark reminder of the urgency. I knew I had to review the records, draft a response, and double-check every figure before the end of the day. But the text from Mia popped up: “Ugh, today was endless. Can you talk?” I could almost hear the exhaustion in her words. As her friend, I wanted to be there, to listen and offer comfort like I always did. But the weight of my professional responsibility pressed down on me. If I didn’t act quickly, the company could face penalties. My fingers hovered over the keyboard, torn between opening the chat window and pulling up the tax files. The expectations from both sides pulled at me, and I felt the familiar knot of anxiety tighten in my chest.
